title: I made this game with Ai, BUUUTTT ..
author: Dismal1021
selftext: But I put a lot of human into it. Alot of iterations. Alot of, take these things out and make it this way. Alot of, hey what's wrong with this, fix it. Paying testers to give me a report on it. Playing it myself alot, thinking about how it can be better, but still keeping it simple .. something to put out and take pride in, that its an actual good game ... I tried to see through others point of views, and I thought, yeah I wouldn't want to play an Ai game either .. but if they put alot of human into it, I actually think I would ... not trying to change anybodies mind, just my thoughts ... I dont know how to create a game all by myself, nor do I have the money to pay someone else to ... I just thought it would be super cool to make one, even with the help of Ai ...I grew up with nintendo, and sega, then Playstations and xboxs .. and I just had a bit of a dream of making a game, and took advantage of the tools out there nowadays .. but I didnt want to put out some slop, thats why I spent months tinkering with it, giving it the human touch .. cause it was slop at first ..  but Ai was like a dev I paid, to get the game right ... anyways

replies.author: Dismal1021
replies.body: Yeah it is like flappy bird .. Just like every other fps game is like the first fps game, etc. I downloaded a flappy bird clone to play it, and it seems way different than my game, but similar

comments.author: NotYourValidation
comments.body:
"I made this game with AI. But I put a lot of human into it."

You mean AI made the game for you, fixed your issues, and gave you game design suggestions.

Look, prompt engineering is a real thing, so I get it. But you technically didn't make anything. I don't go to taco bell, order 20 tacos, go home, and then tell everyone I made dinner. Even if I tell them to add sour cream in it to make it "my own" it's still not made by me. I told someone else to make it, and they did.

I have seen very good AI games with very human game design behind it. Games that you can tell AI actually did take the back seat and was not the main character. I don't see that in your game. Especially not a in a Flappy Bird clone with a gravity-flipping gimmick.

comments.author: credible_human
comments.body:
5.3-xhigh made that for me back in March, down nearly identical graphics, particle effects, physics, basically everything. In 1-2 hours time off a single prompt in codex. I hate to be the bearer of bad news but what you have is not unique at all. Frankly I'm shocked at how near identical yours is to mine.

When my harness shat this out, I considered it a tech demo and moved on to harder projects. I didn't jump on reddit and try to market it. Lmao.

comments.author: Few_Comedian4245
comments.body:
Just checked out the store page and noticed it's a paid game - compared to the hundreds of other free copies of Flappy Bird (I know you have your gravity reversing flip, but still), is there any reason you opted for a premium game instead?

That barrier for entry may put off a lot of potential customers / players

replies.author: Dismal1021
replies.body: I thought .99 cents was pretty cheap for a game, I also recently made it free for like 8 days ... the ai I used suggested I sell it for that price lol

replies.author: Dismal1021
replies.body: Also, I made (prompted) the game cause I really wanted to accomplish having a game on play store .. but I put a price on it, in hopes to help support my family (wife and 7 kids) .. but if not, it was still cool to do it
